notes: Page 2 (step 1): four yellow 1x2 plates placed on the four corners of the black 6x16 plate, each lying along the long axis. Exact stud positions are read from the picture and are approximate.
The '2x' box in the top-left means the whole car is built twice. Only the first copy is recorded here; later pages will show the second copy's pieces, or it should be handled as a repeat.
Page numbering: this is booklet page 2; the parts list covers the full set (366 pieces).
Several MCP connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive) need authorization via claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable and were not used.
Page 3 (step 2): adds 1 yellow Brick 1x4 (b6), 2 yellow Plates 1x2 (b7, b8) and 4 black Brackets (b9-b12) on the black base plate b1. Ids continue from b5 on page 2.

The picture shows only three brackets (front-left, front-right, and one being lowered at back-right). I assumed the 4x box means the fourth sits at back-left, hidden from this view, with one bracket at each corner.

Stud positions on b1 are read from an angled drawing and are approximate. Each bracket's lower flange is assumed to sit on a 2x2 block of b1 studs just inside the corner yellow plates. The upper flanges hang outward past the ends of the plate.
The 1x4 brick and the two loose yellow plates are placed near the middle of the plate, as drawn.
The bracket anti port names (anti.1.x, anti.2.x for the lower flange) are my best guess from the catalogue's 2x5 port layout.
Each bracket rests on b1 only; the corner yellow plates are not under the lower flanges in this reading.
Page 4 (step 3): adds 1 yellow Plate 2x4 (b13), 2 yellow Plates 2x6 (b14, b15) and 4 dark bluish gray grille tiles (b16-b19). Ids continue from b12.
The '2x' sub-assembly is a yellow 2x6 plate with two grille tiles on it. I recorded both copies, with b14 at the left end of the base and b15 at the right end, each across the full width.
Each 2x6 plate sits over the corner yellow plates (b2/b4 on the left, b3/b5 on the right) and the base plate b1. The plate's port anti.r.c maps to b1 column r (1-2 from that end) and row c (1-6).
The 2x4 plate b13 sits in front of the yellow 1x4 brick b6, on top of b7 and part of b8, and on b1. Positions are approximate, read from the angled drawing.
Tile positions on the 2x6 plates (one at each end, on opposite rows) are approximate.
The step 2 brackets are not shown touching the new plates, so no edges to them are added.
Page 5 (step 4): adds 2 dark bluish gray grille tiles (b20, b21), 4 yellow 1x1 bricks (b22-b25) and 1 yellow 1x4 brick (b26). Ids continue from b19.

The drawing shows one 1x1 brick being lowered at the back of the right plate (b24, arrow). I assumed the other three are already placed: b22 and b23 on the left plate, b25 on the right plate, one near each end of each plate.
Exact stud positions of the 1x1 bricks and grille tiles are approximate. The 1x4 brick b26 is placed on the base plate in front of the 2x4 plate b13, at row 5.
The two grille tiles are assumed to sit on the yellow 2x4 plate b13.
Page 6 (step 5): 4 copies of a yellow inverted 45-degree slope 2x1 with a yellow 1x1 plate on its top stud. Ids continue from b26 (slopes b27-b30, plates b31-b34).
Each slope sits on one of the four yellow 1x1 bricks from step 4 (b22-b25), at one end of the slope. The picture shows two near each plate end; I assigned them one per brick.
The catalogue entry for lego-3665 lists only anti ports and no stud ports, so the 1x1 plates are joined to the slopes with no port named on the slope side.
Which stud of the slope the plate sits on, and which slope end rests on the brick, are read from a small inset and are approximate.

Page 7 (step 6): adds 8 yellow 1x2x2 panels (b35-b42), four along the back edge and four along the front edge of the base. The panels form pairs: two 4-stud-long runs per side, one at each end, with a gap in the middle where the yellow 1x4 bricks sit. Ids continue from b34.
Panel positions on b1 are estimated from the angled drawing: columns 3-6 and 11-14, on the back row (row 1) and front row (row 6).

This estimate overlaps the lower flanges of the brackets b9-b12 as I placed them on page 3. Those bracket stud positions were guesses, so I left them unchanged. Treat the real bracket footprint as unresolved.
Each panel is recorded as resting on b1 only.
Page 8 (step 7): adds 4 yellow ladder plates (b43-b46) and 2 yellow 1x4 bricks (b47, b48). Ids continue from b42.
Ladder plates: one at each corner end, hanging outward. The picture shows two being lowered (left-back and right-back) and two already in place at the front. I recorded all four.

Each ladder plate is assumed to clutch the 1x1 plate (b31-b34) and the second stud of the slope below it (b27-b30). The slope has no stud ports in the catalogue, so that side has no port named. The ladder-to-corner assignment is approximate.
The two 1x4 bricks go on top of the middle 1x4 bricks of the back and front walls: b47 on b6 and b48 on b26. This makes the middle section as tall as the panel walls on either side.
The 1x4 stud mapping (b47 on b6, b48 on b26, same columns) is assumed.
Page 9 (step 8): adds 4 black Plates 1x8 (b49-b52) and 2 black Plates 1x2 (b53, b54). Ids continue from b48. They cap the top of the side walls.

Layout of each side wall top: a 1x8 plate, then a 1x2 plate over the middle 1x4 brick, then a 1x8 plate. This is 18 studs, so the ends overhang the 16-stud base over the slopes and ladder plates. The back 1x2 (b53) is the one shown being lowered; the front 1x2 (b54) is assumed already placed, since the drawing shows a continuous front strip.
Assignments: b49 back-left, b50 back-right, b51 front-left, b52 front-right 1x8 plates; b53 back middle and b54 front middle 1x2 plates.
Under each 1x8 plate: a ladder plate, two panels and one end stud of the 1x4 brick. One stud position in each 1x8 plate sits over the gap beside the panels and has no joint.
The exact stud alignment is inferred from the drawing and is approximate.
Page 10 (step 9): adds 2 yellow Plates 1x6 (b55, b56) across the two ends and 4 yellow 1x8 grooved tiles (b57-b60) along the sides. Ids continue from b54.

Layout: the 1x6 end plates sit at the first and last stud of the 18-stud side wall tops, each reaching across the full width. The tiles then cover the remaining 16 studs of each side: two 1x8 tiles per side, meeting over the middle 1x2 plate (b53 at the back, b54 at the front).

Each end plate is recorded as clutching only the end studs of the two side 1x8 plates (b49/b51 on the left, b50/b52 on the right). The drawing shows nothing under its middle section, since the bracket flanges below are lower.
Plate 1x6 port anti.1.1 is the back end and anti.1.6 the front end. Tile stud mapping follows the stud positions assumed on page 9.
Page 11 (step 10): adds 2 black Technic plates 2x4 (b61, b62) and 2 yellow Plates 1x4 (b63, b64). Ids continue from b60. This page is uncertain and the structure below is a best reading.

Inset step 1 shows one black 2x4 flanked by two yellow 1x4 plates. Inset step 2 shows a larger block with a second black plate. I read it as one 6-wide, 4-long layer: yellow 1x4, black 2x4, black 2x4, yellow 1x4 side by side. This matches the 6-stud width of the car end. Only the right end is drawn with an arrow pointing up at the underside of the black bracket flanges; I assume the left end gets the same treatment on a later page.

The layer is pushed up under the two black bracket upper flanges at the right end (b11, b12), stud into anti-stud. I could not tell from the drawing which exact studs engage, so no port is named on the bracket side and the stud port on each new plate is a guess.
The pieces in the layer sit side by side, so they are recorded as contact only.
Alternative reading: one black plate and one yellow plate per end, but the drawing shows two yellow plates around one black plate in step 1.
Page 12 (step 11): adds 1 yellow Plate 4x4 (b65), id continues from b64. It goes on top of the right-hand black bracket flanges (b11 and b12), at the right end of the car.

The yellow plate is drawn covering the right-end overhang. I assume its outer rows rest on the upper flanges of the two brackets, with each bracket covering two of the four rows. The bracket stud mapping (bracket upper flange studs 1.3-1.5 and 2.3-2.5) is a guess, and the fourth stud column of the plate is left unjoined.

The drawing shows only the right end completed. The left end presumably gets a matching plate on a later page, which would use a second 4x4 yellow plate; the parts list has only 2 in total, one per car.

Page 13 (step 12): builds a small flat assembly and pushes it up under the left end of the car. Ids continue from b65. Pieces: Technic plate 2x6 (b66), two yellow 1x6 plates (b67, b68), two black 1x4 plates (b69, b70) and two black 1x2 plates (b71, b72).
Step 1: the yellow 1x6 plates are placed along both long sides of the yellow Technic 2x6 plate (side by side, so contact only), making a 4-wide, 6-long layer.

Step 2: the black plates are placed on top of the Technic plate. The two 1x4 plates sit side by side at one end; the two 1x2 plates sit at the other end, with one being lowered by the arrows. Their exact stud positions are estimated.

The finished assembly goes under the black bracket flanges at the left end (b9, b10). The outer yellow 1x6 plates clutch under the flanges and the Technic plate sits in the gap between them. No bracket port is named because the underside layout is unclear.
The left-end layer here may mirror what steps 10-11 built at the right end. Not verified.
The 6-wide vs 4-wide reading of the page 11 layer is unchanged.
Page 14 (step 13): adds 4 yellow handle tiles (b73-b76) and 1 yellow Plate 4x6 (b77). Ids continue from b72.

The inset piece with the window opening is matched to lego-2432 (Tile Special 1x2 with Handle, yellow). The parts list has 8 of them, so 4 per car fits. The handles stand at the four corners of the car body, on the end plates: b73 and b74 on the left end plate b55, b75 and b76 on the right end plate b56, each at the back and front end of the 6-stud plate.

The yellow 4x6 plate (b77) caps the left-end layer from step 12. It lies over all four pieces of that layer (yellow plates b67 and b68, black plates b69-b72) and is joined to their top studs. The row mapping of the 4x6 plate to the layer pieces is estimated.
The yellow 4x4 plate (b65) already caps the right end.

Page 15 (step 14): adds 2 yellow steering stands (b78 left end, b79 right end), 2 yellow 3x2 sloped bricks (b80 left, b81 right) and 1 black handrail bar 1x4x2 (b82, left end only). Ids continue from b77.

Left end: the handrail goes on the outer edge of the yellow 4x6 plate b77 (across its 4-stud width). The stand and slope sit on b77, stand outward and slope inward. Right end: the slope and stand sit on the yellow 4x4 plate b65 (slope inward, stand outward). There is no handrail on the right end in this step.

Stud positions are approximate. On b77, stud column 1 is taken as the outer end of the car. On b65, columns 1-3 are the inner side (over the bracket flanges) and column 4 the outer end, matching page 12.
Assumption: the steering stand base is 1x2 along the car's width, centred between the two middle rows.

Page 16 (steps 1-2 of a new sub-model): a black bogie, the train undercarriage shown in the preview at top left. It is built separate from the car body, so there are no joins to b1-b82 yet. Ids continue from b82.

Step 1: two black wheel holders (b83, b84) are placed end to end and a dark bluish gray Plate 2x6 (b85) goes on top of both. The catalogue entry for lego-2878c01 lists only axle ports and no studs, so the joins to b85 have no port named on the holder side.
Step 2: a black Train Buffer Beam (b86, inset piece with round buffers) goes on one end of the plate, and a black Plate 1x2 (b87) goes on the plate next to it. The exact stud positions are estimated.
Other pages show the bogie plate (Tile Special 6x4 with pin) and the couplings; they will appear later.
Page 17: step 3 of the bogie plus the first picture of mounting the bogie on the car. Ids continue from b87: magnet b88, coupling b89, bogie plate b90.

Step 3: the black magnet (b88) is pushed into the back of the black train coupling (b89), which then clips onto the buffer-beam end of the bogie (b86). I assumed the magnet goes in the coupling's socket and the coupling's pin joins the buffer beam; the catalogue only lists pin.1 and socket.1 for the coupling and has no ports for the magnet or the buffer beam hook.

The black bogie plate (b90, Tile Special 6x4 with pin) caps the top of the bogie, over the dark gray plate b85 and the black 1x2 plate b87. lego-4025 has only a pin port, so no stud port is named on its underside.

Right half of the page (no step number shown): the car is shown upside down and the bogie's pin goes into a hole of the yellow Technic plate b66 under the left end, next to the handrail b82. This is recorded as a revolute joint, since a train bogie swivels. The circled hole is taken as pin-hole.2 of 5; the numbering direction is a guess.
It is unclear whether this mounting is a separate step or part of step 3. I recorded it because it is shown on this page. The second bogie for the right end is probably built on a later page.
Page 18 (step 15): shows only the finished yellow well-car unit with the black bogie fitted at the left end, labelled '2x'. No new pieces are placed on this page.

The '2x' means this whole unit (pages 2-17) is built twice. The parts list quantities cover both units. Pieces b1-b90 describe the first unit only. The second unit will need a repeat or a second set of ids, depending on how later pages show it.

Page 19: builds a second black bogie, steps 1-3. It has no joins to the car body yet. Ids continue from b90. The preview at the top left shows it with two red axles, which are probably added on the next page.
Step 1: black 1x2 plates b92 and b93 sit across the width at the two ends of the yellow Technic plate 2x8 (b91, the Technic plate with 7 holes).

Step 2: two dark bluish gray round 2x2 plates with axle holes (b94, b95) go on the Technic plate, one left and one right. The catalogue gives lego-4032a only one anti port, so each is joined at a single stud. A black 2x6 plate (b96) crosses the middle of the Technic plate, lying across the car's width.

Step 3: two black wheel holders (b97, b98) fit under the assembly. The catalogue has no stud ports for lego-2878c01, and the picture does not show which part of the Technic plate they clutch, so both joins have no ports named.
The positions of the round plates and the cross plate are read from a small drawing, so they are approximate.
Page 20: steps 4 and 5 of the second bogie started on page 19. Ids continue from b98. Step 4 builds a small underside block and fits it under the bogie. Step 5 adds the top frame and two red axles.

Step 4 (insets 1-3): a black 2x6 plate (b100) is the base, a dark bluish gray 2x4 plate (b99) goes on its middle, and black grille bricks (b101, b102) go on the two end studs. Four black round 1x1 bricks (b103-b106) go on the gray plate, two near each end. I read the insets as this because the gray plate in the insets is overlapped by black studs at its ends. The layout is a best guess from small drawings.

The finished underside block is pushed up into the underside of the bogie. I recorded it as one joint between b100 and the Technic plate b91, with no ports named, because the picture does not show which studs engage.

Step 5: the red axles (b111, b112) go through the axle holes of the round plates b94, b95, which are the only joints recorded for them. A frame of two black 1x6 tiles (b109, b110, along the sides) and two black 1x4 tiles (b107, b108, across the ends) goes around the top of the bogie. The side tiles are joined to the wheel holders b97/b98 and the end tiles to the end plates b92/b93, but these joins are approximate.
The tiles meet each other at the corners of the frame, so they are recorded as contact.

Page 21 (step 16): no new pieces. The second black bogie from pages 19-20 is shared between the two yellow units. The first unit's Technic-plate end (b61, the black Technic 2x4 plate from page 11) is set onto one red axle of the bogie. The axle goes through a Technic hole; I recorded it as the middle hole (pin-hole.2) with a revolute (turning) joint.

The arrow shows the second yellow unit (the other copy from the '2x' on page 18) being lowered onto the other red axle (b112). Pieces of that second unit have not been listed with ids, so its join to b112 is not recorded. It will need its own ids, or a repeat of b1-b82 and the first bogie, once the second unit is enumerated.
Which red axle goes to which unit is a guess; the drawing shows one axle covered and one exposed.
The first unit's other end already has its own bogie (b83-b90) from page 17.
Page 22: starts a new light bluish gray container sub-model, shown in the preview at top left. It is separate from the yellow well car for now. Ids continue from b112.

Step 1: two Plates 2x16 (b113, b114) lie side by side, upside down, with their undersides facing up. Step 2: a Plate 2x4 (b115) bridges the middle of both, and four Plate 2x2 Corners (b116-b119) go at the four corners, the last one shown being lowered. The new pieces are pressed onto the undersides, so each joint is the new piece's stud into the 4x16 plate's anti port.
The 2x16 plates are treated as joined to each other only through the bridging pieces. Their side contact is recorded as contact.

Positions are read from a small angled drawing. The 2x4 plate is assumed to be centred (columns 8-9). The corner plates are assumed to sit at the four corners of the 4x16 area, each using three of its four studs (the catalogue lists four stud ports on the corner plate for this part). The exact corner stud choices and the use of the second row of ports are guesses.
Because the plates are upside down, the port names on b113 and b114 use the same row/column scheme as the catalogue, with b113 as the back two rows and b114 as the front two rows.
Page 23: container steps 3-4. Ids continue from b119. The container is now turned right side up, so the corner plates and the middle 2x4 plate from page 22 show as feet underneath.

Step 3: a light bluish gray Brick 1x8 plus a Brick 1x6 end to end along each long edge: b120 and b121 on the back edge, b122 and b123 on the front edge. They cover columns 3-16 of each outer row, leaving columns 1-2 and the two middle rows of studs open. Step 4: seven 1x2 bricks per side on top of those, with six grille bricks (b124-b135) and one plain 1x2 brick (b136 back, b137 front) per side, in the middle (columns 9-10).
The plain 1x2 bricks are drawn in slightly different positions on the front and back, but I used the same layout on both sides. All stud positions are estimated from small drawings.
On b113 and b114 I used the stud ports of the outer rows (row 1 of b113 and row 2 of b114), now that the plates are the right way up.
The grille bricks on the front wall are drawn with vertical slots and those on the back with horizontal ones, which only reflects how they are drawn. They are the same part type.

Page 24: container steps 5 and 6. Each step adds a layer of plates on top of each long wall: one Plate 1x10 and one Plate 1x4 per side per step, 4 plates in total per step. Ids continue from b137: step 5 is b138-b141, step 6 is b142-b145.

Layout: step 5 back is a 1x10 (cols 3-12) plus a 1x4 (cols 13-16); step 5 front is a 1x4 (cols 3-6) plus a 1x10 (cols 7-16). Step 6 is staggered so the seams do not line up: back is a 1x4 (cols 3-6) plus a 1x10 (cols 7-16); front is a 1x10 (cols 3-12) plus a 1x4 (cols 13-16). The step 5 layout is read from the drawing. The step 6 layout is the staggered pattern, which I inferred because the drawing is not clear about where the seams fall.
Step 5 plates sit on the 1x2 bricks from page 23, using the same column layout. Step 6 plates sit on the step 5 plates.
The 3710 and 4477 plate counts match the parts list: four of each in light bluish gray, all used on this page.

Page 25: container steps 7-8. Ids continue from b145. Step 7 adds the roof: Plate 4x6 (b146) and Plate 4x8 (b147) end to end across the four rows, covering columns 3-16. Step 8 adds the roof surface: a Tile 2x2 (b148), two Plates 2x6 (b149, b150), two Tiles 1x6 (b151, b152) and two Tiles 1x8 (b153, b154).

Roof layout is read from the drawing: the 4x6 plate is at the left and the 4x8 plate at the right. In step 8, a 1x8 tile (cols 3-10) and a 1x6 tile (cols 11-16) run along each outer edge. The two middle rows hold a 2x6 plate (cols 3-8), the 2x2 tile (cols 9-10) and another 2x6 plate (cols 11-16). Both sides use the same tile order. This is approximate.
Only the two outer rows of the roof rest on the step 6 plates. The middle two rows hang over the open centre of the container.
Step 7 stud mapping follows the step 6 layout I inferred on page 24.

Page 26 (step 9): adds four 1x2 roof tiles and the two end doors of the container. Ids continue from b154 for the tiles, b155-b158. The door pieces are in the 'door' repeat (x2), so their ids are door1.<part> and door2.<part>.

Door sub-assembly (labelled 2x): a stack of two Brick 1x4 (brick1 below, brick2 above), with a grille 1x2 brick and two 1x1 handle bricks on top of brick2 (handles at the two end studs, grille in the middle), then a 1x4 tile across the top. This uses the parts list quantities: 4 Brick 1x4, 2 grille bricks, 4 handle bricks and 2 Tile 1x4 across both doors. The drawing seems to show only two layers, so the second Brick 1x4 is an assumption made to use up all the bricks. The 3-brick height does match the rest of the container.

The doors go on the two end faces of the container, with arrows to the left and right ends. Copy 1 sits on column 2 of the base plates (left end). Copy 2 is attached to column 16 (right end) by attach overrides. Only the two middle studs of each door's bottom brick are joined, since the outer rows at the right end already hold the side bricks from page 23.
Placement of the four 1x2 roof tiles is approximate: all on the front-middle row of the two 2x6 roof plates, two on b149 (cols 3-4 and 7-8) and two on b150 (cols 11-12 and 15-16).
The finished drawing also shows a white 'CARGO' sticker on the front wall. The sticker sheet (lego-54290) is not placed in this step, so it is not recorded yet.

Page 27 (step 17): no new bricks. The finished light bluish gray container is lowered into the well of the first yellow unit, and the stickers are applied. The second unit with its bogie is shown joined at the right.
The container's feet (middle 2x4 plate b115 and the four corner plates b116-b119) rest on the well's black base plate b1. Recorded as contact, since the container just sits in the well.

Stickers (sticker sheet b159, one part for the whole sheet) are recorded as stuck to: the 'CARGO' label on the plain 1x2 brick of the container front (b137), the 'TTX' label on the yellow 1x4 brick in the middle of the front wall (b48), the '125T' label on the left front yellow panel (b40), and the small number label on the right front yellow panel (b41). The sticker-to-part mapping is approximate and based on the picture.
The second yellow unit, its brick list and the join to the shared bogie were not recorded with ids earlier. It needs its own set of ids, or a repeat of the first unit, once the later pages are known.
A second container is shown in later steps presumably (double-stack), but is not on this page.

Page 28: starts the blue container, a smaller sibling of the gray container, shown in the preview at top left. The large inset lists the parts for the whole blue container (many are used on later pages). Ids continue from b159.

Step 1: a blue Brick 1x6 on each long edge of the blue Plate 4x8 base (b160). The bricks cover columns 2-7, leaving column 1 and column 8 free at the ends, probably for the end doors on later pages. Step 2: three 1x2 bricks per side: black grille, blue plain, black grille (b163/b167/b164 on the back, b165/b168/b166 on the front). Step 3: a blue Plate 1x6 on top of each side (b169 back, b170 front). The drawing shows one of them already in place and the other being lowered.

The base in the drawing looks two plates thick. The inset also lists blue 2x2 corner plates, a 2x6 plate and 4x6 plate, which are probably feet and roof parts for later steps. The foot structure under the base is not drawn in these steps, so nothing is recorded for it yet.
Layout of the 1x2 bricks along each side is read from the drawing and is approximate.
Black grille bricks: the parts list has 8 in total (black). Four are used here, and the inset shows 6, so two more probably go in the end doors later.

Page 29: blue container steps 4-6. Ids continue from b170. Step 4: blue Plate 4x6 roof (b171) on the two side plates, covering columns 2-7 across the four rows (only the outer rows have support below). Step 5: a blue Tile 1x6 on each outer roof row (b172 front, b173 back); the drawing shows one placed and one being lowered. Steps 1-3 inset (2x) build the end doors, in the 'bdoor' repeat (ids bdoor1.*, bdoor2.*). Step 6 fits one door at each end of the base.

Door sub-assembly (2x): a blue Brick 1x4 with a black grille 1x2 in the middle and a black 1x1 handle brick at each end, then a second blue Brick 1x4 on top, then a blue Tile 1x4. Each door stands on the end column of the base, column 1 for the left door and column 8 for the right door (attach override for copy 2), across all four rows. This fits the base because the side walls only cover columns 2-7.

Correction to the gray container doors on page 26: the same door pattern here shows the order is brick, then the grille-and-handle layer, then a second brick, then the tile. On page 26 I stacked both bricks below the grille layer (brick1, brick2, grille+handles, tile). The correct order for those doors is brick1, grille+handles, brick2, tile. The part set is the same, so only the stacking edges would change.
Parts still unused from the blue inset: 4 blue corner plates, a blue 2x6 plate and 2 blue 1x2 tiles. They are probably feet and roof details, so they may appear on the next page.

Page 30: finishes the blue container (steps 7-8), then shows two more containers with '+' signs, red and white, built the same way. Ids continue from b173: blue corner plates b174-b177, roof tiles b178-b179, 2x6 foot plate b180. The red and white containers are recorded as the 'cont' repeat (2 copies): copy 1 is red (the default colour in the template), copy 2 is white via colour overrides. The ids will be cont1.<id> and cont2.<id>.

Step 7 (upside-down base): four blue 2x2 corner plates go on the underside of the base b160 as feet, the last one shown being lowered. I used three studs per corner plate, and the corners sit at the four corners of the 4x8 base. Step 8: the CARGO sticker goes on the plain blue 1x2 brick on the front of the blue container (b168). The two 1x2 roof tiles (b178, b179) are on the roof's front-middle row at both ends, as on the gray container; the roof tiles are visible in the finished drawing.

The blue 2x6 plate (b180) is a guess: it is in the parts inset but not shown placed in any step. It is placed as a centre foot under rows 2-3 of the base, between the corner plates, similar to the gray container's middle foot. Please recheck against any later page.

The blue inset lists 4 Plate 1x6 (two used for the container sides, b169/b170). The other two are not shown being placed on pages 28-30, so they are left unplaced. The parts list also has 4 blue 3666.

Red and white containers use red or white versions of every part, including the grille bricks, handle bricks, 1x4 bricks and tiles, matching the parts list (red and white 2877, 2921, 3010, 3004, 3009 and so on). Only one sticker sheet exists, so stickers on the red and white containers are not recorded as separate nodes.
All stud positions in these containers are approximate readings from small drawings. The gray container door stack order on page 26 still needs fixing (brick, grille layer, brick, tile).

Page 31 (step 18): no new pieces. This step loads the containers. The red container (cont1) is set on top of the gray container in the first yellow unit. The blue container is stacked on the white container (cont2) in the second yellow unit's well.

Recorded as contact only, since the containers are stacked loosely. Red container feet (cont1.c1-c4 and cont1.foot) rest on the gray container's roof tiles and plate (b149-b154). The blue container's feet (b174-b177, b180) rest on the white container's roof (cont2.ta, cont2.tb, cont2.roof).
The white container sitting in the second unit's well, and the second yellow unit's pieces, are not recorded because the second unit has no ids yet; that join is missing.
Which of the red or white copies is cont1 or cont2 depends on the repeat's copy order: copy 1 is red, copy 2 is white.
Stud-level joins are not needed here because the containers just rest on each other.
Page 32: back cover with a photo of the finished model. No building step, so nothing is added.

Known gaps in the graph so far: (1) the second yellow well-car unit, built per the '2x' on page 18, has no piece ids, so its parts and its joins to the shared bogie and to the white container are missing. (2) Several stud positions and port choices were guesses from small angled drawings; the notes on earlier pages list the main ones. (3) The gray container door stacking on page 26 should be brick, grille+handles layer, brick, tile (as on page 29). (4) Blue 3666 plates (two unplaced), the red and white versions of that part, and the bogie's coupling and axle details are approximate.

The checker's missing-parts list is the full second yellow well-car unit: the booklet's first-page '2x' means the whole well car (pages 2-18) is built twice, and my earlier pages only recorded the first copy. The unit is now added as the repeat 'unit2' (one copy, ids unit2.b1 to unit2.b90), a copy of the first unit including its own end bogie. The graph is not a separate model.

Type count fix for the black 1x2 plates: the parts list has 8 lego-3023 black and 4 lego-32028 (Plate Special 1x2 with Door Rail, black). The first unit's ids b87, b92 and b93 (the plates on the bogies) are most likely the door-rail plates 32028, because those are the plates the bogie steps use, and unit 1's four other black 1x2 plates (b53, b54, b71, b72) are really plain 3023. To make the totals match the list without editing earlier ids, the second unit's b53, b54, b71, b72 are typed lego-32028 and its end-bogie plate b87 is lego-3023. Totals then match: 3023 black 8, 32028 4. The real type of each individual plate is uncertain from the drawings.

The second unit's piece positions repeat the first unit's. Its Technic end (b61/b62, b66) takes the shared bogie's second red axle (b112): the joint b112 to unit2.b61 pin-hole.2. Its other end has its own bogie (unit2.b83-b90) with the pin in unit2.b66.
The white container (cont2) rests on the second unit's base (contact edges to unit2.b1), mirroring the red one on the first unit. The blue container sits on the white one (recorded earlier).

Plate 1x6 totals: the parts list has 4 each in blue, red and white; I had only placed 2 per colour. The other two in each colour (b181-b186) are placed under each container's centre foot plate, stacked to make the feet two plates thick. This is a guess because pages 28-30 do not show them clearly. For red and white they join cont1.foot and cont2.foot.

The gray container doors (page 26) still have the wrong stacking order noted before (brick, brick, grille layer, tile instead of brick, grille layer, brick, tile). Only the stack edges would change; the part counts are unaffected.

Cause of the two groups: the second yellow unit is the repeat group 'unit2' with times=1. Per the naming rule, copies are named <group><n>, so its parts are unit21.b1 ... unit21.b90, not unit2.b1. My earlier joints to 'unit2.b61' and 'unit2.b1' pointed at ids that do not exist, so the second unit (with the white and blue containers on it) looked cut off from the first.

Fix: the same joints are repeated here with the correct ids. The shared bogie's second red axle b112 goes into unit21.b61's Technic hole (pin-hole.2, revolute), and the white container (cont2) rests on unit21.b1. The earlier 'unit2.*' edges are wrong duplicates and can be ignored; they cannot be removed in an additions-only reply.
This is one train car built from two yellow well-car units joined by the shared bogie, so the build is a single connected model, not separate models.

Connection chain now: first unit (b1-b82, its bogie b83-b90) - shared bogie b91-b112 - second unit (unit21.*), with the gray container (b113-b154), the red container (cont1) and the sticker on the first unit, and the white (cont2) and blue (b160-b186) containers on the second.

Plate Round 2 x 2 with Axle Hole

notes: Page 2 (step 1): four yellow 1x2 plates placed on the four corners of the black 6x16 plate, each lying along the long axis. Exact stud positions are read from the picture and are approximate.
The '2x' box in the top-left means the whole car is built twice. Only the first copy is recorded here; later pages will show the second copy's pieces, or it should be handled as a repeat.
Page numbering: this is booklet page 2; the parts list covers the full set (366 pieces).
Several MCP connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive) need authorization via claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable and were not used.
Page 3 (step 2): adds 1 yellow Brick 1x4 (b6), 2 yellow Plates 1x2 (b7, b8) and 4 black Brackets (b9-b12) on the black base plate b1. Ids continue from b5 on page 2.

The picture shows only three brackets (front-left, front-right, and one being lowered at back-right). I assumed the 4x box means the fourth sits at back-left, hidden from this view, with one bracket at each corner.

Stud positions on b1 are read from an angled drawing and are approximate. Each bracket's lower flange is assumed to sit on a 2x2 block of b1 studs just inside the corner yellow plates. The upper flanges hang outward past the ends of the plate.
The 1x4 brick and the two loose yellow plates are placed near the middle of the plate, as drawn.
The bracket anti port names (anti.1.x, anti.2.x for the lower flange) are my best guess from the catalogue's 2x5 port layout.
Each bracket rests on b1 only; the corner yellow plates are not under the lower flanges in this reading.
Page 4 (step 3): adds 1 yellow Plate 2x4 (b13), 2 yellow Plates 2x6 (b14, b15) and 4 dark bluish gray grille tiles (b16-b19). Ids continue from b12.
The '2x' sub-assembly is a yellow 2x6 plate with two grille tiles on it. I recorded both copies, with b14 at the left end of the base and b15 at the right end, each across the full width.
Each 2x6 plate sits over the corner yellow plates (b2/b4 on the left, b3/b5 on the right) and the base plate b1. The plate's port anti.r.c maps to b1 column r (1-2 from that end) and row c (1-6).
The 2x4 plate b13 sits in front of the yellow 1x4 brick b6, on top of b7 and part of b8, and on b1. Positions are approximate, read from the angled drawing.
Tile positions on the 2x6 plates (one at each end, on opposite rows) are approximate.
The step 2 brackets are not shown touching the new plates, so no edges to them are added.
Page 5 (step 4): adds 2 dark bluish gray grille tiles (b20, b21), 4 yellow 1x1 bricks (b22-b25) and 1 yellow 1x4 brick (b26). Ids continue from b19.

The drawing shows one 1x1 brick being lowered at the back of the right plate (b24, arrow). I assumed the other three are already placed: b22 and b23 on the left plate, b25 on the right plate, one near each end of each plate.
Exact stud positions of the 1x1 bricks and grille tiles are approximate. The 1x4 brick b26 is placed on the base plate in front of the 2x4 plate b13, at row 5.
The two grille tiles are assumed to sit on the yellow 2x4 plate b13.
Page 6 (step 5): 4 copies of a yellow inverted 45-degree slope 2x1 with a yellow 1x1 plate on its top stud. Ids continue from b26 (slopes b27-b30, plates b31-b34).
Each slope sits on one of the four yellow 1x1 bricks from step 4 (b22-b25), at one end of the slope. The picture shows two near each plate end; I assigned them one per brick.
The catalogue entry for lego-3665 lists only anti ports and no stud ports, so the 1x1 plates are joined to the slopes with no port named on the slope side.
Which stud of the slope the plate sits on, and which slope end rests on the brick, are read from a small inset and are approximate.

Page 7 (step 6): adds 8 yellow 1x2x2 panels (b35-b42), four along the back edge and four along the front edge of the base. The panels form pairs: two 4-stud-long runs per side, one at each end, with a gap in the middle where the yellow 1x4 bricks sit. Ids continue from b34.
Panel positions on b1 are estimated from the angled drawing: columns 3-6 and 11-14, on the back row (row 1) and front row (row 6).

This estimate overlaps the lower flanges of the brackets b9-b12 as I placed them on page 3. Those bracket stud positions were guesses, so I left them unchanged. Treat the real bracket footprint as unresolved.
Each panel is recorded as resting on b1 only.
Page 8 (step 7): adds 4 yellow ladder plates (b43-b46) and 2 yellow 1x4 bricks (b47, b48). Ids continue from b42.
Ladder plates: one at each corner end, hanging outward. The picture shows two being lowered (left-back and right-back) and two already in place at the front. I recorded all four.

Each ladder plate is assumed to clutch the 1x1 plate (b31-b34) and the second stud of the slope below it (b27-b30). The slope has no stud ports in the catalogue, so that side has no port named. The ladder-to-corner assignment is approximate.
The two 1x4 bricks go on top of the middle 1x4 bricks of the back and front walls: b47 on b6 and b48 on b26. This makes the middle section as tall as the panel walls on either side.
The 1x4 stud mapping (b47 on b6, b48 on b26, same columns) is assumed.
Page 9 (step 8): adds 4 black Plates 1x8 (b49-b52) and 2 black Plates 1x2 (b53, b54). Ids continue from b48. They cap the top of the side walls.

Layout of each side wall top: a 1x8 plate, then a 1x2 plate over the middle 1x4 brick, then a 1x8 plate. This is 18 studs, so the ends overhang the 16-stud base over the slopes and ladder plates. The back 1x2 (b53) is the one shown being lowered; the front 1x2 (b54) is assumed already placed, since the drawing shows a continuous front strip.
Assignments: b49 back-left, b50 back-right, b51 front-left, b52 front-right 1x8 plates; b53 back middle and b54 front middle 1x2 plates.
Under each 1x8 plate: a ladder plate, two panels and one end stud of the 1x4 brick. One stud position in each 1x8 plate sits over the gap beside the panels and has no joint.
The exact stud alignment is inferred from the drawing and is approximate.
Page 10 (step 9): adds 2 yellow Plates 1x6 (b55, b56) across the two ends and 4 yellow 1x8 grooved tiles (b57-b60) along the sides. Ids continue from b54.

Layout: the 1x6 end plates sit at the first and last stud of the 18-stud side wall tops, each reaching across the full width. The tiles then cover the remaining 16 studs of each side: two 1x8 tiles per side, meeting over the middle 1x2 plate (b53 at the back, b54 at the front).

Each end plate is recorded as clutching only the end studs of the two side 1x8 plates (b49/b51 on the left, b50/b52 on the right). The drawing shows nothing under its middle section, since the bracket flanges below are lower.
Plate 1x6 port anti.1.1 is the back end and anti.1.6 the front end. Tile stud mapping follows the stud positions assumed on page 9.
Page 11 (step 10): adds 2 black Technic plates 2x4 (b61, b62) and 2 yellow Plates 1x4 (b63, b64). Ids continue from b60. This page is uncertain and the structure below is a best reading.

Inset step 1 shows one black 2x4 flanked by two yellow 1x4 plates. Inset step 2 shows a larger block with a second black plate. I read it as one 6-wide, 4-long layer: yellow 1x4, black 2x4, black 2x4, yellow 1x4 side by side. This matches the 6-stud width of the car end. Only the right end is drawn with an arrow pointing up at the underside of the black bracket flanges; I assume the left end gets the same treatment on a later page.

The layer is pushed up under the two black bracket upper flanges at the right end (b11, b12), stud into anti-stud. I could not tell from the drawing which exact studs engage, so no port is named on the bracket side and the stud port on each new plate is a guess.
The pieces in the layer sit side by side, so they are recorded as contact only.
Alternative reading: one black plate and one yellow plate per end, but the drawing shows two yellow plates around one black plate in step 1.
Page 12 (step 11): adds 1 yellow Plate 4x4 (b65), id continues from b64. It goes on top of the right-hand black bracket flanges (b11 and b12), at the right end of the car.

The yellow plate is drawn covering the right-end overhang. I assume its outer rows rest on the upper flanges of the two brackets, with each bracket covering two of the four rows. The bracket stud mapping (bracket upper flange studs 1.3-1.5 and 2.3-2.5) is a guess, and the fourth stud column of the plate is left unjoined.

The drawing shows only the right end completed. The left end presumably gets a matching plate on a later page, which would use a second 4x4 yellow plate; the parts list has only 2 in total, one per car.

Page 13 (step 12): builds a small flat assembly and pushes it up under the left end of the car. Ids continue from b65. Pieces: Technic plate 2x6 (b66), two yellow 1x6 plates (b67, b68), two black 1x4 plates (b69, b70) and two black 1x2 plates (b71, b72).
Step 1: the yellow 1x6 plates are placed along both long sides of the yellow Technic 2x6 plate (side by side, so contact only), making a 4-wide, 6-long layer.

Step 2: the black plates are placed on top of the Technic plate. The two 1x4 plates sit side by side at one end; the two 1x2 plates sit at the other end, with one being lowered by the arrows. Their exact stud positions are estimated.

The finished assembly goes under the black bracket flanges at the left end (b9, b10). The outer yellow 1x6 plates clutch under the flanges and the Technic plate sits in the gap between them. No bracket port is named because the underside layout is unclear.
The left-end layer here may mirror what steps 10-11 built at the right end. Not verified.
The 6-wide vs 4-wide reading of the page 11 layer is unchanged.
Page 14 (step 13): adds 4 yellow handle tiles (b73-b76) and 1 yellow Plate 4x6 (b77). Ids continue from b72.

The inset piece with the window opening is matched to lego-2432 (Tile Special 1x2 with Handle, yellow). The parts list has 8 of them, so 4 per car fits. The handles stand at the four corners of the car body, on the end plates: b73 and b74 on the left end plate b55, b75 and b76 on the right end plate b56, each at the back and front end of the 6-stud plate.

The yellow 4x6 plate (b77) caps the left-end layer from step 12. It lies over all four pieces of that layer (yellow plates b67 and b68, black plates b69-b72) and is joined to their top studs. The row mapping of the 4x6 plate to the layer pieces is estimated.
The yellow 4x4 plate (b65) already caps the right end.

Page 15 (step 14): adds 2 yellow steering stands (b78 left end, b79 right end), 2 yellow 3x2 sloped bricks (b80 left, b81 right) and 1 black handrail bar 1x4x2 (b82, left end only). Ids continue from b77.

Left end: the handrail goes on the outer edge of the yellow 4x6 plate b77 (across its 4-stud width). The stand and slope sit on b77, stand outward and slope inward. Right end: the slope and stand sit on the yellow 4x4 plate b65 (slope inward, stand outward). There is no handrail on the right end in this step.

Stud positions are approximate. On b77, stud column 1 is taken as the outer end of the car. On b65, columns 1-3 are the inner side (over the bracket flanges) and column 4 the outer end, matching page 12.
Assumption: the steering stand base is 1x2 along the car's width, centred between the two middle rows.

Page 16 (steps 1-2 of a new sub-model): a black bogie, the train undercarriage shown in the preview at top left. It is built separate from the car body, so there are no joins to b1-b82 yet. Ids continue from b82.

Step 1: two black wheel holders (b83, b84) are placed end to end and a dark bluish gray Plate 2x6 (b85) goes on top of both. The catalogue entry for lego-2878c01 lists only axle ports and no studs, so the joins to b85 have no port named on the holder side.
Step 2: a black Train Buffer Beam (b86, inset piece with round buffers) goes on one end of the plate, and a black Plate 1x2 (b87) goes on the plate next to it. The exact stud positions are estimated.
Other pages show the bogie plate (Tile Special 6x4 with pin) and the couplings; they will appear later.
Page 17: step 3 of the bogie plus the first picture of mounting the bogie on the car. Ids continue from b87: magnet b88, coupling b89, bogie plate b90.

Step 3: the black magnet (b88) is pushed into the back of the black train coupling (b89), which then clips onto the buffer-beam end of the bogie (b86). I assumed the magnet goes in the coupling's socket and the coupling's pin joins the buffer beam; the catalogue only lists pin.1 and socket.1 for the coupling and has no ports for the magnet or the buffer beam hook.

The black bogie plate (b90, Tile Special 6x4 with pin) caps the top of the bogie, over the dark gray plate b85 and the black 1x2 plate b87. lego-4025 has only a pin port, so no stud port is named on its underside.

Right half of the page (no step number shown): the car is shown upside down and the bogie's pin goes into a hole of the yellow Technic plate b66 under the left end, next to the handrail b82. This is recorded as a revolute joint, since a train bogie swivels. The circled hole is taken as pin-hole.2 of 5; the numbering direction is a guess.
It is unclear whether this mounting is a separate step or part of step 3. I recorded it because it is shown on this page. The second bogie for the right end is probably built on a later page.
Page 18 (step 15): shows only the finished yellow well-car unit with the black bogie fitted at the left end, labelled '2x'. No new pieces are placed on this page.

The '2x' means this whole unit (pages 2-17) is built twice. The parts list quantities cover both units. Pieces b1-b90 describe the first unit only. The second unit will need a repeat or a second set of ids, depending on how later pages show it.

Page 19: builds a second black bogie, steps 1-3. It has no joins to the car body yet. Ids continue from b90. The preview at the top left shows it with two red axles, which are probably added on the next page.
Step 1: black 1x2 plates b92 and b93 sit across the width at the two ends of the yellow Technic plate 2x8 (b91, the Technic plate with 7 holes).

Step 2: two dark bluish gray round 2x2 plates with axle holes (b94, b95) go on the Technic plate, one left and one right. The catalogue gives lego-4032a only one anti port, so each is joined at a single stud. A black 2x6 plate (b96) crosses the middle of the Technic plate, lying across the car's width.

Step 3: two black wheel holders (b97, b98) fit under the assembly. The catalogue has no stud ports for lego-2878c01, and the picture does not show which part of the Technic plate they clutch, so both joins have no ports named.
The positions of the round plates and the cross plate are read from a small drawing, so they are approximate.
Page 20: steps 4 and 5 of the second bogie started on page 19. Ids continue from b98. Step 4 builds a small underside block and fits it under the bogie. Step 5 adds the top frame and two red axles.

Step 4 (insets 1-3): a black 2x6 plate (b100) is the base, a dark bluish gray 2x4 plate (b99) goes on its middle, and black grille bricks (b101, b102) go on the two end studs. Four black round 1x1 bricks (b103-b106) go on the gray plate, two near each end. I read the insets as this because the gray plate in the insets is overlapped by black studs at its ends. The layout is a best guess from small drawings.

The finished underside block is pushed up into the underside of the bogie. I recorded it as one joint between b100 and the Technic plate b91, with no ports named, because the picture does not show which studs engage.

Step 5: the red axles (b111, b112) go through the axle holes of the round plates b94, b95, which are the only joints recorded for them. A frame of two black 1x6 tiles (b109, b110, along the sides) and two black 1x4 tiles (b107, b108, across the ends) goes around the top of the bogie. The side tiles are joined to the wheel holders b97/b98 and the end tiles to the end plates b92/b93, but these joins are approximate.
The tiles meet each other at the corners of the frame, so they are recorded as contact.

Page 21 (step 16): no new pieces. The second black bogie from pages 19-20 is shared between the two yellow units. The first unit's Technic-plate end (b61, the black Technic 2x4 plate from page 11) is set onto one red axle of the bogie. The axle goes through a Technic hole; I recorded it as the middle hole (pin-hole.2) with a revolute (turning) joint.

The arrow shows the second yellow unit (the other copy from the '2x' on page 18) being lowered onto the other red axle (b112). Pieces of that second unit have not been listed with ids, so its join to b112 is not recorded. It will need its own ids, or a repeat of b1-b82 and the first bogie, once the second unit is enumerated.
Which red axle goes to which unit is a guess; the drawing shows one axle covered and one exposed.
The first unit's other end already has its own bogie (b83-b90) from page 17.
Page 22: starts a new light bluish gray container sub-model, shown in the preview at top left. It is separate from the yellow well car for now. Ids continue from b112.

Step 1: two Plates 2x16 (b113, b114) lie side by side, upside down, with their undersides facing up. Step 2: a Plate 2x4 (b115) bridges the middle of both, and four Plate 2x2 Corners (b116-b119) go at the four corners, the last one shown being lowered. The new pieces are pressed onto the undersides, so each joint is the new piece's stud into the 4x16 plate's anti port.
The 2x16 plates are treated as joined to each other only through the bridging pieces. Their side contact is recorded as contact.

Positions are read from a small angled drawing. The 2x4 plate is assumed to be centred (columns 8-9). The corner plates are assumed to sit at the four corners of the 4x16 area, each using three of its four studs (the catalogue lists four stud ports on the corner plate for this part). The exact corner stud choices and the use of the second row of ports are guesses.
Because the plates are upside down, the port names on b113 and b114 use the same row/column scheme as the catalogue, with b113 as the back two rows and b114 as the front two rows.
Page 23: container steps 3-4. Ids continue from b119. The container is now turned right side up, so the corner plates and the middle 2x4 plate from page 22 show as feet underneath.

Step 3: a light bluish gray Brick 1x8 plus a Brick 1x6 end to end along each long edge: b120 and b121 on the back edge, b122 and b123 on the front edge. They cover columns 3-16 of each outer row, leaving columns 1-2 and the two middle rows of studs open. Step 4: seven 1x2 bricks per side on top of those, with six grille bricks (b124-b135) and one plain 1x2 brick (b136 back, b137 front) per side, in the middle (columns 9-10).
The plain 1x2 bricks are drawn in slightly different positions on the front and back, but I used the same layout on both sides. All stud positions are estimated from small drawings.
On b113 and b114 I used the stud ports of the outer rows (row 1 of b113 and row 2 of b114), now that the plates are the right way up.
The grille bricks on the front wall are drawn with vertical slots and those on the back with horizontal ones, which only reflects how they are drawn. They are the same part type.

Page 24: container steps 5 and 6. Each step adds a layer of plates on top of each long wall: one Plate 1x10 and one Plate 1x4 per side per step, 4 plates in total per step. Ids continue from b137: step 5 is b138-b141, step 6 is b142-b145.

Layout: step 5 back is a 1x10 (cols 3-12) plus a 1x4 (cols 13-16); step 5 front is a 1x4 (cols 3-6) plus a 1x10 (cols 7-16). Step 6 is staggered so the seams do not line up: back is a 1x4 (cols 3-6) plus a 1x10 (cols 7-16); front is a 1x10 (cols 3-12) plus a 1x4 (cols 13-16). The step 5 layout is read from the drawing. The step 6 layout is the staggered pattern, which I inferred because the drawing is not clear about where the seams fall.
Step 5 plates sit on the 1x2 bricks from page 23, using the same column layout. Step 6 plates sit on the step 5 plates.
The 3710 and 4477 plate counts match the parts list: four of each in light bluish gray, all used on this page.

Page 25: container steps 7-8. Ids continue from b145. Step 7 adds the roof: Plate 4x6 (b146) and Plate 4x8 (b147) end to end across the four rows, covering columns 3-16. Step 8 adds the roof surface: a Tile 2x2 (b148), two Plates 2x6 (b149, b150), two Tiles 1x6 (b151, b152) and two Tiles 1x8 (b153, b154).

Roof layout is read from the drawing: the 4x6 plate is at the left and the 4x8 plate at the right. In step 8, a 1x8 tile (cols 3-10) and a 1x6 tile (cols 11-16) run along each outer edge. The two middle rows hold a 2x6 plate (cols 3-8), the 2x2 tile (cols 9-10) and another 2x6 plate (cols 11-16). Both sides use the same tile order. This is approximate.
Only the two outer rows of the roof rest on the step 6 plates. The middle two rows hang over the open centre of the container.
Step 7 stud mapping follows the step 6 layout I inferred on page 24.

Page 26 (step 9): adds four 1x2 roof tiles and the two end doors of the container. Ids continue from b154 for the tiles, b155-b158. The door pieces are in the 'door' repeat (x2), so their ids are door1.<part> and door2.<part>.

Door sub-assembly (labelled 2x): a stack of two Brick 1x4 (brick1 below, brick2 above), with a grille 1x2 brick and two 1x1 handle bricks on top of brick2 (handles at the two end studs, grille in the middle), then a 1x4 tile across the top. This uses the parts list quantities: 4 Brick 1x4, 2 grille bricks, 4 handle bricks and 2 Tile 1x4 across both doors. The drawing seems to show only two layers, so the second Brick 1x4 is an assumption made to use up all the bricks. The 3-brick height does match the rest of the container.

The doors go on the two end faces of the container, with arrows to the left and right ends. Copy 1 sits on column 2 of the base plates (left end). Copy 2 is attached to column 16 (right end) by attach overrides. Only the two middle studs of each door's bottom brick are joined, since the outer rows at the right end already hold the side bricks from page 23.
Placement of the four 1x2 roof tiles is approximate: all on the front-middle row of the two 2x6 roof plates, two on b149 (cols 3-4 and 7-8) and two on b150 (cols 11-12 and 15-16).
The finished drawing also shows a white 'CARGO' sticker on the front wall. The sticker sheet (lego-54290) is not placed in this step, so it is not recorded yet.

Page 27 (step 17): no new bricks. The finished light bluish gray container is lowered into the well of the first yellow unit, and the stickers are applied. The second unit with its bogie is shown joined at the right.
The container's feet (middle 2x4 plate b115 and the four corner plates b116-b119) rest on the well's black base plate b1. Recorded as contact, since the container just sits in the well.

Stickers (sticker sheet b159, one part for the whole sheet) are recorded as stuck to: the 'CARGO' label on the plain 1x2 brick of the container front (b137), the 'TTX' label on the yellow 1x4 brick in the middle of the front wall (b48), the '125T' label on the left front yellow panel (b40), and the small number label on the right front yellow panel (b41). The sticker-to-part mapping is approximate and based on the picture.
The second yellow unit, its brick list and the join to the shared bogie were not recorded with ids earlier. It needs its own set of ids, or a repeat of the first unit, once the later pages are known.
A second container is shown in later steps presumably (double-stack), but is not on this page.

Page 28: starts the blue container, a smaller sibling of the gray container, shown in the preview at top left. The large inset lists the parts for the whole blue container (many are used on later pages). Ids continue from b159.

Step 1: a blue Brick 1x6 on each long edge of the blue Plate 4x8 base (b160). The bricks cover columns 2-7, leaving column 1 and column 8 free at the ends, probably for the end doors on later pages. Step 2: three 1x2 bricks per side: black grille, blue plain, black grille (b163/b167/b164 on the back, b165/b168/b166 on the front). Step 3: a blue Plate 1x6 on top of each side (b169 back, b170 front). The drawing shows one of them already in place and the other being lowered.

The base in the drawing looks two plates thick. The inset also lists blue 2x2 corner plates, a 2x6 plate and 4x6 plate, which are probably feet and roof parts for later steps. The foot structure under the base is not drawn in these steps, so nothing is recorded for it yet.
Layout of the 1x2 bricks along each side is read from the drawing and is approximate.
Black grille bricks: the parts list has 8 in total (black). Four are used here, and the inset shows 6, so two more probably go in the end doors later.

Page 29: blue container steps 4-6. Ids continue from b170. Step 4: blue Plate 4x6 roof (b171) on the two side plates, covering columns 2-7 across the four rows (only the outer rows have support below). Step 5: a blue Tile 1x6 on each outer roof row (b172 front, b173 back); the drawing shows one placed and one being lowered. Steps 1-3 inset (2x) build the end doors, in the 'bdoor' repeat (ids bdoor1.*, bdoor2.*). Step 6 fits one door at each end of the base.

Door sub-assembly (2x): a blue Brick 1x4 with a black grille 1x2 in the middle and a black 1x1 handle brick at each end, then a second blue Brick 1x4 on top, then a blue Tile 1x4. Each door stands on the end column of the base, column 1 for the left door and column 8 for the right door (attach override for copy 2), across all four rows. This fits the base because the side walls only cover columns 2-7.

Correction to the gray container doors on page 26: the same door pattern here shows the order is brick, then the grille-and-handle layer, then a second brick, then the tile. On page 26 I stacked both bricks below the grille layer (brick1, brick2, grille+handles, tile). The correct order for those doors is brick1, grille+handles, brick2, tile. The part set is the same, so only the stacking edges would change.
Parts still unused from the blue inset: 4 blue corner plates, a blue 2x6 plate and 2 blue 1x2 tiles. They are probably feet and roof details, so they may appear on the next page.

Page 30: finishes the blue container (steps 7-8), then shows two more containers with '+' signs, red and white, built the same way. Ids continue from b173: blue corner plates b174-b177, roof tiles b178-b179, 2x6 foot plate b180. The red and white containers are recorded as the 'cont' repeat (2 copies): copy 1 is red (the default colour in the template), copy 2 is white via colour overrides. The ids will be cont1.<id> and cont2.<id>.

Step 7 (upside-down base): four blue 2x2 corner plates go on the underside of the base b160 as feet, the last one shown being lowered. I used three studs per corner plate, and the corners sit at the four corners of the 4x8 base. Step 8: the CARGO sticker goes on the plain blue 1x2 brick on the front of the blue container (b168). The two 1x2 roof tiles (b178, b179) are on the roof's front-middle row at both ends, as on the gray container; the roof tiles are visible in the finished drawing.

The blue 2x6 plate (b180) is a guess: it is in the parts inset but not shown placed in any step. It is placed as a centre foot under rows 2-3 of the base, between the corner plates, similar to the gray container's middle foot. Please recheck against any later page.

The blue inset lists 4 Plate 1x6 (two used for the container sides, b169/b170). The other two are not shown being placed on pages 28-30, so they are left unplaced. The parts list also has 4 blue 3666.

Red and white containers use red or white versions of every part, including the grille bricks, handle bricks, 1x4 bricks and tiles, matching the parts list (red and white 2877, 2921, 3010, 3004, 3009 and so on). Only one sticker sheet exists, so stickers on the red and white containers are not recorded as separate nodes.
All stud positions in these containers are approximate readings from small drawings. The gray container door stack order on page 26 still needs fixing (brick, grille layer, brick, tile).

Page 31 (step 18): no new pieces. This step loads the containers. The red container (cont1) is set on top of the gray container in the first yellow unit. The blue container is stacked on the white container (cont2) in the second yellow unit's well.

Recorded as contact only, since the containers are stacked loosely. Red container feet (cont1.c1-c4 and cont1.foot) rest on the gray container's roof tiles and plate (b149-b154). The blue container's feet (b174-b177, b180) rest on the white container's roof (cont2.ta, cont2.tb, cont2.roof).
The white container sitting in the second unit's well, and the second yellow unit's pieces, are not recorded because the second unit has no ids yet; that join is missing.
Which of the red or white copies is cont1 or cont2 depends on the repeat's copy order: copy 1 is red, copy 2 is white.
Stud-level joins are not needed here because the containers just rest on each other.
Page 32: back cover with a photo of the finished model. No building step, so nothing is added.

Known gaps in the graph so far: (1) the second yellow well-car unit, built per the '2x' on page 18, has no piece ids, so its parts and its joins to the shared bogie and to the white container are missing. (2) Several stud positions and port choices were guesses from small angled drawings; the notes on earlier pages list the main ones. (3) The gray container door stacking on page 26 should be brick, grille+handles layer, brick, tile (as on page 29). (4) Blue 3666 plates (two unplaced), the red and white versions of that part, and the bogie's coupling and axle details are approximate.
